verdict: NEGATIVE. group_floor_sim stays 0.0. Three values cleared arms A/B/C (0.45 best at +19.0 pt on the schema-aware drifting arm, with B +1.0 and C +0.7), and every one of them loses 8.3-13.9 pt on the 3-persona chat set. The two values that cost the chat set nothing (0.65, 0.70) buy +2.0 and -1.0 on arm A, i.e. nothing. This independently reproduces the engine's own recorded finding with an arm its authors did not have.
note: corrects temporal_drift_results.json, which dismissed this sweep on an arm whose tags come from the lexical tagger. The floor defect reproduces with PERFECT tags, so it is independent of tagger recall.
chat_regression_added: floor_retune_spec.md defined arms A/B/C only. engine._apply_group_floor records that three earlier fixes 'cost more on the 3-persona chat set than they gained', so that set was measured BEFORE any default was changed, to judge this candidate on the same evidence as the old ones. It was added as an additional hurdle, never as a replacement for a clause that failed.
what_the_split_shows: arm A gives records an EXPLICIT correct entity; the chat set lets the TAGGER infer one. 0.45 is +19.0 on the first and -13.9 on the second. The floor is compensating for tagger precision, and a single global threshold cannot serve both a caller that declares its schema and a tagger guessing from prose. Whether the floor should depend on tag PROVENANCE is a separate hypothesis, and is not claimed by this result.
